pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is **/boddhisattva/** ​— ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

Phoneme ​by ​phoneme:

- ‌**boddhisattva** — ​The ‌canonical ​restored ‌form Bodhisattva.

​For ​the ​modern speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: Read ‌"Bodhisattva" ​using ‌the reconstructed ​pronunciation ‌above; ​the ‌conventional Latin ​spelling ​adds ‌no diacritic ‌marks.

‌The ​conventional ​spelling "Bodhisattva" ‌is ​already ​written in ‌Latin ​letters; ​the ‌lowercase form ​"boddhisattva" ‌differs ​only ​in capitalization.

​The ​pronunciation ‌given above ‌reconstructs ​the ‌sound ​world in ​which ‌Bodhisattva ‌was invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should ‌not expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not a ​performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌reconstructed pronunciation ​of ‌Bodhisattva ​is explained ‌separately ‌from ​its ​conventional Latin ​spelling, ​which ‌adds no ‌diacritic ​marks.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Bodhisattva ‌place enlightenment ​being, ​compassion at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

### ​Origins ‌(Myth)

Bodhisattva ​appears ‌in buddhist ​tradition ‌as enlightenment ​being, ​compassion. The ​name's ​meaning, "'Awakening-being' ​— ‌one who ​vows ‌Buddhahood for ​the ‌sake of ​all ‌beings", shapes ​the ‌narratives told ​about ​this figure.

### ‌Worship ‌and ‌Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ​and later ‌tradition-keepers ​preserved Bodhisattva ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name survived ‌into ​the modern ​scholarly ​record.

The ​myths ‌of Bodhisattva ‌survive ​in fragments, ‌summaries, ​and ​later retellings. ‌Each ‌version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ​its ‌tellers — ​poets, ​priests, philosophers, ​and ‌scholars. The ​PuniCodex ​entry does ​not ‌privilege a ​single ​version; it ​gathers ‌the attestations ​so ‌that readers ​can ‌compare ​them. The ‌restoration ‌Bodhisattva gives ​the ​figure a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Bodhisattva ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Buddhist ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming बोधिसत्त्व, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to enlightenment ​being ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

overview.body:
**Bodhisattva** ​(*boddhisattva*) — ‌Enlightenment Being, ‌Compassion · ​'Awakening-being' — ​one ​who vows ​Buddhahood for ​the sake ‌of all ​beings ​— belongs ‌to the ​Buddhist tradition, ‌where it ​is ‌catalogued under ​the domain ​"Enlightenment Being, ​Compassion". The ​name ​means "'Awakening-being' ‌— one ​who vows ‌Buddhahood ​for the ‌sake of ​all beings"[^1].

‌A **bodhisattva** ​is ‌a being ​who has ​vowed **awakening ‌for the ‌sake ‌of all ​beings** — ​and who, ‌by that ​vow, ​defers the ‌exit: not ​final nirvāṇa ​while a ‌single ​being remains ‌unliberated. The ​Mahāyāna made ​the word ​its ​founding institution: ‌the bridge ‌from one ​man's awakening ‌to ​a vocation ​open to ‌everyone.[^2]

PuniCodex ‌records the ‌canonical ‌scholarly spelling ​**Bodhisattva** and ‌serves its ​temple at ​[its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/boddhisattva/). The ‌displayed form ​is ASCII-equivalent ​— ​a description ‌computed from ​the displayed ​form itself. ​The ‌plain ASCII ​form *boddhisattva* ‌contains the ​same letters: ‌no ​recovered diacritics ‌or special ‌encoding is ​claimed. The ​work ​here is ​consistent citation, ‌capitalization, provenance, ‌and cultural ​context[^3].

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Devanagari as ​**बोधिसत्त्व**. ​Etymologically it ​means "'Awakening-being' ​— one ​who ‌vows Buddhahood ​for the ​sake of ‌all beings"[^1].

​The ‌canonical spelling ​**Bodhisattva** matches ‌the conventional ​scholarly ​romanization. The ​plain ASCII ​form *boddhisattva* ​contains ‌the same ​letters, so ‌no lost ​diacritics ‌or encoding ​transition is ‌claimed. The ​editorial ‌work is ​to fix ​one reviewed ‌reference spelling, ‌preserve ‌capitalization and ​provenance, and ​keep the ‌original ​evidence visible. ​The displayed ‌form is ​ASCII-equivalent ​— a ‌description computed ​from the ‌displayed ​form itself.

​The letter-by-letter ​transformation runs:

- ​**b** ‌→ **B** ‌— Same, ​capitalized
- **o** ‌→ ​**o** — ​Same
- **d** ‌→ **d** ‌— Same
- ‌**d** ‌→ **h** ​— Special ‌character
- **h** ​→ ​**i** — ​Special character
- ‌**i** → ​**s** ​— Special ​character
- **s** ‌→ **a** ​— ​Special character
- ​**a** → ‌**t** — ​Special ‌character
- **t** ​→ **t** ‌— Same
- ​**t** → ‌**v** ‌— Special ​character
- **v** ​→ **a** ​— ​Special character
- ‌**a** → ‌**—** — ​Dropped

meditation.body:
The ​bodhisattva is ‌the most ‌daring ​idea in ​the history ​of ​ethics: a ​moral agent ‌whose ​deadline is ​**infinity**. Ordinary ‌virtue balances ​cost ‌and reward; ​the vow ‌sets ​the reward ​aside entirely ​— ​awakening withheld, ​deliberately, until ‌the ​last stranger ‌is free. ​Logically ‌it is ​madness; existentially ‌it ​is the ‌only response ​to ​a world ‌of uncountable ‌suffering that ‌does ​not end ​in despair ‌or ​indifference.

And ​yet the ‌tradition ​is unsentimental ​about it. ‌The ​vow does ‌not float; ​it ​climbs — ​six perfections, ​ten ‌stages, three ‌incalculable eons. ​Compassion ‌without method ​is just ​grief, the ‌masters ‌said, and ‌method without ‌compassion ​is just ‌cold. The ​bodhisattva ​holds both: ​the tenderness ‌of ​Avalokiteśvara and ​the terrifying ​patience ‌of Kṣitigarbha, ​still standing ​in ​the doorway ‌of hell, ​in ‌no hurry ​to leave. ‌The word ​asks ‌of everyone ‌who hears ​it ​the simplest ​and hardest ​question: ‌**who are ‌you waiting ​for?**[^1]
